data.title: Node.js
data.tagline: A runtime for JavaScript outside the browser, often used by local scripts and build tools
data.learningOutcome: You can recognize a missing or outdated node installation and use node -v to check whether the local version meets the project requirement.
data.description: When a project specifies a Node.js version, use node -v in the terminal to check your local runtime. Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser and can provide local capabilities such as file-system access; browser scripts run in a page environment, which is different.

learning.assumes: You have heard of JavaScript and seen projects require an installed environment.
learning.outcome: You can recognize a missing or outdated node installation and use node -v to check whether the local version meets the project requirement.

distinctions.label: Browser
distinctions.explanation: A browser also runs JavaScript, but scripts live with the page and stop when it closes. Node.js runs independently in a terminal without opening a web page.

distinctions.label: npm
distinctions.explanation: npm is the tool that installs packages, and it runs on Node.js. When node reports command not found, installing Node.js comes before using npm.

explanation.title: It is a runtime, not a new language
explanation.text: You still write JavaScript. Node.js adds the ability to execute it on a computer, so scripts run without opening a browser.

explanation.title: Build and package tools depend on it
explanation.text: npm and many project build commands use Node.js; whether a project needs it depends on its toolchain. Commands that rely on a missing Node.js installation report command not found.

explanation.title: Projects require specific versions
explanation.text: When docs say requires Node 18+, run node -v to see the local version; upgrade before running if it is too low.

data.boundary: Node.js does not replace the browser: in-page interactions still run there. It adds the ability to run JavaScript outside the browser, which command-line tools and server programs rely on.

lessonPractice.title: Following project docs, running npm start reports command not found: node. What should happen next?

options.label: Install Node.js, verify the version with node -v, then retry
options.feedback: Correct. npm runs on Node.js, and whether build commands depend on it varies by toolchain. The version also needs to meet the project requirement.

options.label: Re-clone the project and run the same command
options.feedback: The error says this machine lacks the node program; it has nothing to do with whether the project files are complete.

options.label: Open the project entry file in a browser to run it
options.feedback: A browser runs only page scripts; it cannot replace the Node.js runtime the project needs.

data.agentPrompt: The terminal reports command not found: node. First check whether Node.js is installed here and its version; if it is missing or below the project requirement, tell me which version to install, then rerun the project command and confirm it starts.
